findings.summary: commit 927383b2 introduces a new zip() call without strict= in the new finite_bracket() helper, adding two lint findings (B905, RUF007) not present in the baseline revision, and no pre-stage ruff pass was run on the touched file

the new test file tests/test_exact_clip_seed_bracket.py has an unsorted import block (ruff I001); tests/ is excluded from the repo's default lint scope so this would not surface in a normal path-scoped check unless the file is named explicitly

justifications.durability: tests/test_exact_clip_seed_bracket.py directly constructs the real 342-cell carrier under exact-clip mode and asserts the booked amplitude is finite and within 1e-2 of unity - this exercises the actual fixed code path on genuine solver-scale data rather than a synthetic bracket, which is a stronger regression guard than a mocked fixture would be, and I independently confirmed it passes. It is correctly marked @pytest.mark.slow per the repo's marker policy for numerical/JAX-JIT tests, so it will not run in the bare default `pytest` lane and needs `-m "slow or not slow"` or explicit selection to fire - consistent with how the project already gates its other expensive equilibrium tests, not a defect specific to this landing. The one process gap noted under fit (missed lint pass introducing two new findings) is a minor, mechanically-fixable durability cost rather than a correctness one.
justifications.evidence: every number in the manifest and the doc records traces to a log on disk that I read directly: prechange-342-reproduction.log reproduces the exact pre-change refusal text; negative-fixed-endpoints.log shows the same a(0)=nan/a(1)=0.89683512 refusal when only the fixed-endpoint mutation is restored (96.92s, 1 failed as declared); final-combined-all-debug-rerun.log carries both SEED_BRACKET_ROW JSON lines verbatim matching the manifest's artifacts field and the evidence table's numbers exactly, followed by the LLVM allocation failure and then '4 passed in 274.37s' from a fresh process. The measurement script (measure_seed_brackets.py, read directly) embeds its own self-check - it raises AssertionError before printing a row if the amplitude is off-tolerance, the chord digest does not match the pre-change reference, or the wall-level shift is not uniform to 8 eps - so the two printed SEED_BRACKET_ROW lines are independent confirmation of those three properties, not just a claim. All three reviewed commits are read directly via git show (none are ancestors of this review worktree's HEAD, consistent with how these worktree-local commits are handled elsewhere in this sprint) and git show --stat on each matches changed_paths with nothing extra. I also independently reran tests/test_exact_clip_seed_bracket.py in the target node's own still-clean, still-on-commit worktree (UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=~/Code/nova/.venv PYTHONPATH=$PWD uv run --no-sync pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_exact_clip_seed_bracket.py -v) and independently got '1 passed in 378.07s' at exit 0 - slower than the node's own combined 274.37s (no warm compile cache on this rerun) but the identical pass outcome on the identical 342-cell construction.
justifications.fit: git show --stat on all three commits lists exactly nova/equilibrium/forward.py, tests/test_exact_clip_seed_bracket.py, docs/plans/exact-clip-moment-quadrature.html and docs/evidence/archive/exact-clip-moment-quadrature-landed.html - matching changed_paths with nothing extra; nova/equilibrium/forward_operator.py is confirmed untouched as the manifest claims. No plan, sprint or ticket label appears in any commit message, symbol or comment, and the two open plan decisions (fallback-fence-norm, traced-vertex-capacity-for-multi-run-cells) are correctly left alone - the 1072-cell LLVM failure is explicitly NOT attributed to the open traced-vertex-capacity decision, which is the right call since it never produced a multi-run-cell receipt. Set against that: the repo's own committing procedure requires a path-scoped `ruff check --fix` pass on touched files before staging, and this was skipped for the touched region of forward.py - the new finite_bracket() helper's `zip(finite, finite[1:])` is flagged B905 and RUF007 on the final revision where it was clean at baseline, a small but real process gap in an otherwise disciplined landing.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the declared defect - the exact cold seed's fixed 0/1 amplitude bracket refusing with a(0)=nan on the real 342-cell carrier even though a finite sign-changing interval exists inside (0,1) - is reproduced bit-for-bit pre-change (prechange-342-reproduction.log: 'ValueError: exact clip seed boundary level does not bracket unit amplitude: a(0)=nan, a(1)=0.89683512') and is fixed post-change: the 110/135 and 300/342 rows both construct finite amplitudes within the 1% tolerance (1.00579, 1.00925) with bit-identical chord-mode seeds (chord_bit_identical=true against the pre-change reference digest for both rows) and a uniform wall-level shift within 8 float64 eps. The mechanism is correctly diagnosed and explained in the evidence record (two nested quadratic-profile cut cells inside an inner compact bank of capacity one poison the current vector at fraction 0 despite nonempty outer support). The one gap: the largest declared reference size (1000 requested / 1072 realised cells) never reached a seed verdict - it hit an unrelated LLVM 'Cannot allocate memory' compilation failure in the shared all_debug allocation before the bracket logic could be exercised at that scale - so the fix is demonstrated on two of the three sizes named in the open work, with the third an honestly reported measurement negative rather than a silently dropped case.
justifications.scope_discipline: the three commits touch only the four files named above; the ephemeral measurement driver (measure_seed_brackets.py) was correctly kept out of the repository under the run's own directory rather than committed as throwaway benchmark code, and no other in-flight §3 node's files were touched. follow_ons correctly defers the 1072-cell compiler-memory negative to coordinator disposition rather than either quietly dropping it or overclaiming it as a fix.

SCORE goal_fidelity: 19
JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: the declared defect is reproduced pre-change and fixed post-change on the 110/135 and 300/342 rows with finite amplitudes within 1% tolerance, bit-identical chord seeds, and a uniform wall-level shift within 8 eps; the mechanism (two nested cut cells inside an inner compact bank of capacity one poisoning the current vector) is correctly diagnosed. The gap: the largest declared size (1000/1072) never reached a seed verdict due to an unrelated LLVM allocation failure, so the fix is demonstrated on two of three sizes, honestly reported rather than dropped.
SCORE evidence: 20
JUSTIFICATION evidence: every number in the manifest and doc records traces to a log I read directly, including a self-validating measurement script that raises before printing a row if amplitude, chord digest or wall-uniformity checks fail. I independently reran tests/test_exact_clip_seed_bracket.py in the target's own untouched worktree and got '1 passed in 378.07s' at exit 0, matching the node's own claimed pass outcome on the identical construction.
SCORE fit: 17
JUSTIFICATION fit: git show --stat on all three commits matches changed_paths exactly, forward_operator.py is confirmed untouched, no plan/sprint labels leak into code, and both open plan decisions are correctly left alone. Against that: the repo's committing procedure requires a path-scoped ruff --fix pass before staging, and this was skipped for forward.py - the new finite_bracket() helper introduces two new lint findings (B905, RUF007) not present at baseline.
SCORE scope_discipline: 20
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: the three commits touch only the four declared files; the ephemeral measurement driver was correctly kept out of the repository; no other in-flight node's files were touched; follow_ons correctly defers the 1072-cell negative rather than dropping or overclaiming it.
SCORE durability: 19
JUSTIFICATION durability: the new test constructs the real 342-cell carrier under exact-clip mode and asserts on genuine solver output, a stronger guard than a synthetic fixture, and I independently confirmed it passes; it is correctly marked slow per the project's existing marker policy for JAX-JIT numerical tests, consistent with how other expensive equilibrium tests are already gated. The missed lint pass is a minor, mechanically-fixable cost rather than a correctness gap.
